messages:
maria-rt: Heads up — I just captured an nsys run (~2s) that shows weird kernel switching when KV cache hit-rate climbs past ~90%. Where should I upload the trace? It may contain short customer prompt tokens in the host-side buffers.

josh-kernel: Upload to the internal perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/traces/private/. Prefer a scrubbed tarball (gz) and put an accompanying metadata file. Don’t make public. Naming: <ts>-<model>-<seq>-kv-<tag>.nsys.tar.gz e.g. 1765432100-llama2-2048-kv-high.nsys.tar.gz.

ev an-profiling: quick checklist: remove raw prompt text, redact S3 paths/keys, strip IPs/hostnames, remove user IDs. If you can’t fully redact, put the trace into a restricted folder and mention the ticket.

josh-kernel: nsys capture example we use (feel free to trim):

```bash
NSYS_OUTPUT=perf-1765432100
nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,cudnn --output ${NSYS_OUTPUT} --force --sample=none 
  -- python -u run_infer.py --model llama2 --seq_len 2048 --batch 1

# then convert to timeline for perfetto viewer
nsys-ui ${NSYS_OUTPUT}.nsys-rep --export=timeline ${NSYS_OUTPUT}-timeline.json
```

josh-kernel: After capture:
- run perf-scrub.sh on the .nsys-rep (this strips env vars, hostnames, and small prompt blobs)
- create a metadata file 'meta.txt' with driver/cuda/kernel/model/config
- tar + gpg sign if it’s customer-sensitive

maria-rt: How do we annotate KV cache events so the timeline shows hits/misses?

josh-kernel: Add a small annotations JSON next to the trace named <nsys>-annotations.json. Minimal example (one-line in slack):

```json
[ { "ts_ms": 1765432100123, "type": "kv_hit", "key": "prefix_42", "lat_ms": 0.12 },
  { "ts_ms": 1765432100789, "type": "kv_miss", "key": "prefix_43", "lat_ms": 2.1 } ]
```

Then in perfetto load timeline JSON and import annotations; we have a tiny viewer script at tools/viewer/add_annotations.py if you need help. Prefix events with kv_ so reviewers can grep.

evan-profiling: Also include these fields in meta.txt as plain lines (helps triage): kernel: <version>, nvidia-driver: <version>, cuda: <version>, python: <version>, commit: <git sha>, batching-config: <json-snippet>.

ops-bot: Reminder — set object ACL to internal-only and tag the S3 object with 'sensitivity=redacted' or 'sensitivity=private'. If trace contains customer data, create an internal ticket and attach the S3 path, do not share link in external channels.

sara-sre: For perf-regressions: attach a baseline trace and include a one-paragraph summary of the delta (e.g., kernel X increased latency 3x when seq=2048). If possible upload a short 10–20 line stack summary of the top kernels (we use `nsys stats` -> top_kernels.txt).

josh-kernel: small scrub example (use conservatively):

```bash
# remove prompt-like strings and s3 paths from the timeline json
cat perf-1765432100-timeline.json | jq 'walk(if type=="string" then sub("s3://[^"]+"; "S3_REDACTED")|sub("[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{40,}";"TOKEN_REDACTED") else . end)' > perf-1765432100-timeline-scrub.json

# quick tar+gzip
tar -czf 1765432100-llama2-2048-kv-high.nsys.tar.gz perf-1765432100* meta.txt perf-1765432100-annotations.json
```

maria-rt: thanks — I’ll scrub and upload to s3://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/traces/private/1765432100-llama2-2048-kv-high.nsys.tar.gz and ping the infra ticket #INF-1629. Any preference on who reviews KV timeline?

josh-kernel: tag @evan-profiling and @sara-sre; I’ll look at kernel selection heuristics after you upload. Also include the exact batching/caching config used (we've tripped over a few heuristics that flip at >128 requests/sec).

evan-profiling: If you suspect a regression, run the same capture with the previous runtime commit hash and include both tarballs. We run a diff job that highlights kernel time deltas automatically.

maria-rt: done, uploading now. thanks :thumbsup:
